items.headline: 10-year note auction ($42bn, 11-10): high yield 5.020%, 1.0 bp tail vs WI 5.010% (biggest tail since February; six-month average a 0.6 bp stop-through), bid-to-cover 2.46 (lowest since May), indirects 61.2% (lowest since Oct 2023, -19.1 pts), directs 29.0% (highest since Sep 2013), dealers 9.8%
items.source: TheStreet Pro 'Stock Market Today: November 10, 2026' (Neil Sethi, 11-10 15:47 ET); HERE Rock Hill (11-11 06:51); helious.io auction table; Gokhshtein Media (11-10, qualitative); all read by WebFetch
items.claim: The Treasury sold $42bn of 10-year notes on 2026-11-10 at a high yield of 5.020%, 1.0 bp above the 5.010% when-issued yield, the biggest tail since February and ending two straight stop-throughs (October: 1.7 bp stop-through; six-month average: 0.6 bp stop-through); the high yield was the lowest since September (October reopening: 5.300%, highest since November 2000). Bid-to-cover fell to 2.46 from 2.77 (lowest since May; six-month average 2.60) on about $103.3bn of bids; indirects took 61.2% versus 80.3% in October, a 19.1-point drop that is the largest auction-to-auction decline since July 2016 and the lowest share since October 2023; directs took 29.0% (highest since September 2013; October 17.1%); dealers 9.8% (most since May; October 2.5%). Median yield 4.961%, 95% allotted at the high. The 10-year yield traded back under 5% (4.988%) after the sale.
items.note: Tail of 1.0 bp is below the 2 bp hard-event threshold. Two independent numbered sources agree (TheStreet, HERE Rock Hill); helious.io shows '+1.0bp' tail and verdict WEAK. The task brief's helious '0.6 bp stop-through' reading was not what the table showed at fetch time; 0.6 bp is TheStreet's six-month average stop-through. HERE Rock Hill dates the indirect low 'since at least October 2025' vs TheStreet 'since October 2023' (not reconciled). Gokhshtein ('widest tail since February', 'international demand collapsed') prints no figures. 30-year ($25bn) is 11-12.

items.candidate_dial: repriced IPO (Anthropic) - range set below earlier targets; demand reports point the other way
items.claim: In an amended filing on 2026-11-10 Anthropic set a price range of $70-78 for 825m Class A shares (plus a 123.75m-share option), a base raise of $57.75-64.35bn, with estimated net proceeds of $84.6-93.7bn including a $26bn private placement of Class N stock to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC (Google and Nvidia $10bn each); the top of the range implies a fully diluted valuation of $1.404tn, below the roughly $2tn reportedly targeted a couple of months earlier and the $1.5tn discussed in early November, but above the $1.1-1.3tn some buyers discussed on 11-06; last private valuation $965bn (May); run-rate revenue $81bn at end-October; ticker ANT on Nasdaq, trading expected close to 11-19. On 11-11 Cailian Press (and FT-attributed copies) reported underwriters are weighing a valuation target of $1.5tn or higher on 'exceptionally strong investor demand'.
items.note: The range itself is the dated new fact (filed). Whether it is a 'repricing' depends on the baseline: down vs $2tn/$1.5tn, up vs the 11-06 Bloomberg $1.1-1.3tn chatter already recorded. The 11-11 above-range reports are secondary copies (PANews cites Cailian Press; mlq.ai/Benzinga copies attributing FT failed to fetch) and had not been confirmed by a filing at run time. 456X Nov 10 also notes 'any downsized volume or discounted pricing will necessitate a reset' as a hypothetical. Low-end valuation ~$1.26tn is from 456X's filing-based figure, not TechCrunch.

items.claim: On 2026-11-10 SoftBank Group reported a July-September net loss of ¥1,115.3bn ($7.0bn), including a ¥597.2bn ($3.73bn) loss at subsidiary Silver Bands 7 from revising its procurement plans for power-generation equipment for US AI data centres, citing 'the evolving requirements of its existing and planned projects': about $2.85bn of non-refundable advances for factory capacity and equipment no longer in its plans (roughly 30% of ¥1,500.9bn / $9.48bn cumulative payments to September 30) and about $0.88bn of contract modifications and settlements payable from Q3 onward; conditional rebates of up to $2.1bn over ten years on future purchases were not booked; about $6.6bn of advances remain allocated to equipment for the PORTS-Pike (Ohio) campus and other projects, and the CFO said PORTS-Pike is not being downsized. items.candidate_dial: capex digestion language (neocloud: CRWV) - NOT a capex cut; FY26 capex raised
items.claim: CoreWeave reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3,661m (vs $1,365m a year earlier), backlog of about $132.5bn, Q3 purchases of property and equipment of $9,441m (above guidance on pull-forward of Q4 deliveries) and raised the low end of FY2026 capex guidance to $37-39bn from $35-39bn; net interest expense was $846m (vs $310m) with Q4 guided to $1.05-1.15bn and weighted average cost of debt 7.9%. On the call management said 2027 capex would 'remain in line with our 2026 capex investment' if it builds only committed backlog, that it retains 'flexibility in how quickly we execute', is 'choosing to be patient' and has not brought 2028 capacity to market 'because we are waiting for that to season further', and that it 'will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to', with asset-level secured loans trading around par and the next DDTL expected at a 7-7.5% yield; about $9bn of customer prepayments and deposits are expected in the next three months. Shares rose 5.7% after hours to $51.51 after closing at $48.73 (-0.51%).
items.sweep_query: 3. capex cut OR deferral OR digestion AI (and ticker sweep CRWV)

No delays, deferrals, customer pushouts or contract renegotiations were reported ('no material risks to our 2027 deliveries'); expiring fleet re-contracting at premiums.
